articles.headline: The PNP opens a nationwide hunt as Bato dela Rosa's surrender week ends
articles.descriptionHtml: The one-week surrender window Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla set on October 23 closed on Friday, October 30, without Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa turning himself in. Task force leader Lt. Gen. Wilson Joseph Lopez told a Camp Crame briefing the police had stood up tracker teams in every region, that Bureau of Immigration records showed the senator had not left the country, and that no surrender feelers had arrived; spokesperson Col. Allen Rae Co had said the day before the ₱50-million reward is for verified tips, not for civilians to make an arrest. Dela Rosa's counsel Israelito Torreon on October 31 again argued that an International Criminal Court warrant is not a Philippine arrest order, and ABS-CBN reported the camp had asked the Supreme Court on Wednesday to stop the arrest after the bounty, in the senator's words, put his life in "serious danger." A week that began as an ultimatum ended as an open manhunt for a sitting senator.

articles.headline: House prosecutors say the unexplained-wealth record is hard to rebut
articles.descriptionHtml: House impeachment adviser Robert Ace Barbers told an October 27 briefing the panel expects a "bloodbath" when Vice President Sara Duterte's defense opens on November 9, and said the remaining unexplained-wealth charge rests on bank, tax and corporate records the Vice President and her husband themselves submitted. "Can you change bank records? Can a witness dispute those ending balances?" he asked, after prosecutors had already dropped confidential funds, bribery and grave threats. On October 29 he warned the defense not to turn its right to present evidence into delay — "not a numbers game" of extra witnesses — and to stay on Article II rather than reopen withdrawn articles. The trial's next move is no longer a new charge but whether the defense can explain the documents already on the table.

articles.headline: The Senate pledges to strip lump-sum funds from the 2027 budget
articles.descriptionHtml: Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian told Super Radyo dzBB on Sunday, October 25, that the Senate will strip lump-sum funds from the ₱7.2-trillion 2027 budget because the Supreme Court has said appropriations cannot exceed the President's proposal, while keeping unprogrammed appropriations inside the Court's parameters — a slice he put at about 2% to 5%. He said SAGIP had been a large lump-sum line in the voided 2024 and 2025 laws and that foreign-assisted subway and railway funding, shifted into unprogrammed appropriations, still needs a careful look. At a Senate finance hearing on October 26 the People's Budget Coalition told senators more than ₱1 trillion of the House bill still looks like patronage: ₱695 billion in "hard pork" infrastructure, ₱210 billion in "soft pork" aid, and ₱112 billion in standby "shadow pork." Last week's ruling is now a drafting rule: the Senate says it will write a 2027 budget the Court will not strike.

articles.headline: A DPWH engineer says Romualdez was not on the kickback proponent list
articles.descriptionHtml: DPWH Bulacan First District engineer Carlo Rivera told the Sandiganbayan Third Division on October 27 that former Speaker Martin Romualdez was not among the flood-control project proponents tied to about ₱5 billion in contractor "commitment" fees he said he collected for then-district engineer Henry Alcantara and passed to then-appropriations chair Zaldy Co. Asked by defense counsel to confirm the omission, Rivera said yes, and named Co, former undersecretary Roberto Bernardo, Senator Jinggoy Estrada and former Senator Ramon "Bong" Revilla Jr. as the proponents Alcantara had identified. He said he also contacted contractors — including Topnotch Catalyst Builders, ARL Builders, Wawao Builders, IM Construction Corp. and SYMS Construction Trading — for those fees from 2022 to 2025. A prosecution witness in the ₱7.4-billion plunder bail hearing described a cash trail that, on this day's testimony, does not run through Romualdez's name.

articles.headline: The peso breaks ₱64 as Marcos tells the public not to panic
articles.descriptionHtml: The peso closed at ₱64.17 per dollar on Tuesday, October 27, 22 centavos weaker than Monday's ₱63.95 and the first finish through ₱64, after an intraday low of ₱64.20, according to Bankers Association of the Philippines data. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. told reporters in Muntinlupa the next day not to panic, blamed higher oil and fuel prices, and said the government would "defend the peso as hard as we possibly can" with what he called healthy reserves; the currency then recovered 14.5 centavos to ₱64.025 and, by Friday, ₱63.74. The break of ₱64 came days after a 50-basis-point Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas hike to 5.5% that Governor Eli Remolona Jr. had said was for inflation, not the exchange rate. A record print is now a public promise to defend the currency, not a reversal of the slide.

articles.headline: The AFP counts 54 Chinese ships in the West Philippine Sea, up from 31
articles.descriptionHtml: The Armed Forces said it monitored 54 Chinese navy and coast guard ships around four West Philippine Sea features from October 20 to 26, up from 31 the week before: seven PLAN and seven China Coast Guard vessels at Ayungin Shoal, six and 11 at Bajo de Masinloc, five and two at Escoda Shoal, and four and 12 at the Pag-asa Islands. West Philippine Sea spokesperson Rear Adm. Roy Vincent Trinidad separately said a Liaoning carrier group that passed the western seaboard and came within 15 miles of land was a twice-yearly exercise and "no cause for alarm," even after the carrier did not answer radio challenges. Last week's completed Ayungin run now sits beside a weekly count that has nearly doubled.

articles.headline: Saudi repatriations climb toward 675 as more OFWs come home
articles.descriptionHtml: OWWA Administrator Patricia Yvonne Caunan said on October 26 that 360 overseas Filipino workers had already come home from Saudi Arabia after the October 10 attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and that 675 had asked to be repatriated, even though the airport had reopened without restoring Manila flights. She said the Department of Migrant Workers was moving workers four to 11 hours to other airports and that Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac was on his way to lead the airlift. By Friday night Cacdac himself landed at NAIA Terminal 3 with 62 more returnees, bringing the official count to 574, and said about 500 more were expected within four to five days. Last week's first 34 is now a multi-hundred airlift that still has no Riyadh–Manila flight.
